exam.subject: Physics
exam.title: Physics 2002

parts.title: Part I – Multiple Choice Questions
parts.instructions: Part I of the paper contains 45 questions worth 1.5 points each. This file keeps only items whose stem, options and answer were verified from the scan.

source.scan: HP Scan image PDF; Part I MCQs read from page images

exam.answer_key_note: No official key in the PDF. Answers solved independently. Skipped: Q7 and Q9 (figures), Q15 (computed focal length not among printed options), Q20 (thermometer-liquid claim not reliable), Q29 and Q38 (circuit/wire figures), Q37 (Bernoulli pressure not among printed options). Part II not included.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is not a unit of force?
explanation_steps: Newton, kg·m·s⁻², g·cm·s⁻² (the dyne) and J/m are all force units.
W·m·s = J·m = N·m², which is not a force. Answer: E.

questions.stem: All of the following quantities are derived quantities except
explanation_steps: Speed, density and volume are derived from base units.
Luminous intensity (the candela) is an SI base quantity. Answer: A.

questions.stem: The volume of an aluminium body X is twice the volume of another aluminium body Y. What can you say about the masses of the two bodies?

options.A: The mass of Y is greater than the mass of X.
options.B: The mass of X is greater than the mass of Y.
options.C: The mass of X and the mass of Y are equal.
options.D: The masses of X and Y are not comparable.

explanation_steps: Both bodies are aluminium, so they have the same density.
Mass = density × volume, and the volume of X is twice the volume of Y, so the mass of X is greater. Answer: B.

questions.stem: A vector has an x-component of 50 units. Find the y-component and the resultant respectively if the resultant makes an angle of 30° with the y-axis. (cos 30° = 0.866, sin 30° = 0.5)
explanation_steps: An angle of 30° with the y-axis means the x-component is R sin 30°.
50 = R × 0.5, so R = 100 units. The y-component is R cos 30° = 86.6 units. Answer: D.

questions.stem: A man walks 40 m due east, then 50 m due north, then 60 m due west. Find the magnitude and direction of the resultant. (tan⁻¹ 0.4 = 21.8°)
explanation_steps: Net displacement is 20 m west and 50 m north.
Magnitude = √(20² + 50²) = √2900 = 53.85 m. The direction is tan⁻¹(20/50) = 21.8° west of north. Answer: B.

questions.stem: A ball is thrown vertically upward at 60 m/s. One second later, at the same place, another ball is projected upward at 130 m/s. At what time after the second ball is thrown, and at what height, do they meet?
explanation_steps: Take g = 9.8 m/s² and let t be the time after the second throw.

questions.stem: A red ball of mass 2 kg moving at 4 m/s in the positive x-direction makes an elastic head-on collision with a white ball of mass 4 kg moving at 5 m/s in the negative x-direction. The final velocities of the red and white balls are respectively
explanation_steps: For a one-dimensional elastic collision, v1 = (m1−m2)u1/(m1+m2) + 2m2 u2/(m1+m2).
That gives v_red = −8 m/s and v_white = 1 m/s. Answer: E.

questions.stem: The ideal mechanical advantage of a simple machine is always

options.A: greater than the actual mechanical advantage.
options.B: less than the actual mechanical advantage.
options.C: equal to the actual mechanical advantage.
options.D: dependent on the nature of the simple machine.
options.E: sometimes greater than and sometimes less than the actual mechanical advantage.

explanation_steps: Efficiency = AMA/IMA and is less than 1 when friction is present.
Therefore IMA is greater than AMA. Answer: A.

questions.stem: When light falls on the surface separating two media, which of the following can happen?

options.A: A portion of the incident light passes into the second medium.
options.B: A portion of the incident light is reflected back with an amplified signal.
options.C: A portion of the incident light is absorbed by the second medium.

explanation_steps: At an interface, light may be transmitted and absorbed.
Reflection does not amplify the signal, so B is false. Answer: D.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about light?

options.A: The law of reflection states that the angle of incidence equals the angle of refraction.
options.B: If rays start from a point and spread in different directions, the beam is called a converging beam.
options.C: A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon passes between the Earth and the Sun.
options.D: Light travels in a straight line when it crosses the interface between two media.

explanation_steps: A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon is between the Earth and the Sun.
The other statements confuse reflection with refraction, a diverging beam with a converging beam, or ignore refraction at an interface. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a ray rule used to find the image formed by a curved mirror?

options.A: A ray parallel to the principal axis passes through the focus after reflection from a concave mirror.
options.B: A ray directed at the centre of curvature is reflected back along itself for a convex mirror.
options.C: A ray through the focus of a concave mirror proceeds parallel to the principal axis after reflection.
options.D: A ray parallel to the principal axis passes through the centre of curvature after reflection from a convex mirror.
options.E: None of the above is used.

explanation_steps: A ray parallel to the principal axis of a convex mirror appears to come from the focus, not from the centre of curvature.
The other listed rules are standard mirror constructions. Answer: D.

questions.stem: A glass rod (n = 1.65) in air has its left end ground to a convex hemisphere of radius 4 cm. A point source is 8 cm to the left of the vertex. Where does the image appear?
explanation_steps: Use n2/v − n1/u = (n2−n1)/R with u = −8 cm and R = +4 cm.
1.65/v − 1/(−8) = 0.65/4, so v = 44 cm to the right of the vertex. Answer: D.

questions.stem: The angles of incidence and refraction for a ray passing from a material into air are 45° and 60°. The refractive index of the material is (sin 45° = 0.707, sin 60° = 0.866)
explanation_steps: n sin 45° = 1 × sin 60°.

questions.stem: A ray of wavelength 6.0×10⁻⁷ m travels from air into glass of refractive index 1.45 at 40° to the normal. Which statement is not correct?

options.A: The speed of the ray in the glass is 2.07×10⁸ m/s.
options.B: The angle of refraction is less than the angle of incidence.
options.C: The wavelength of the ray in the glass is 4.14×10⁻⁷ m.
options.D: The frequency of the ray in the glass is 5×10¹⁴ Hz.
options.E: The frequency of the ray is 3.45×10¹⁴ Hz.

explanation_steps: Speed, wavelength and frequency in glass are c/n = 2.07×10⁸ m/s, λ/n = 4.14×10⁻⁷ m and c/λ = 5×10¹⁴ Hz. Refraction bends toward the normal.
3.45×10¹⁴ Hz is not the frequency. Answer: E.

questions.stem: Which statement is wrong concerning the human eye and a photographic camera?

options.A: Both have a converging lens forming a real, inverted and diminished image on a screen.
options.B: The camera lens has a fixed focal length, but the eye lens can change shape.
options.C: The camera image forms on film and the eye image forms on the retina.
options.D: A camera diaphragm controls the aperture, while the iris controls the pupil.

explanation_steps: Each of A–D is a standard similarity or difference between the eye and a camera.
None of those statements is wrong. Answer: E.

questions.stem: What temperature on the Fahrenheit scale is equal to twice the corresponding Celsius temperature?
explanation_steps: Set F = 2C and F = (9/5)C + 32.
2C = (9/5)C + 32 gives C = 160 and F = 320°F. Answer: C.

questions.stem: An iron block 10 cm × 25 cm × 8 cm has a mass of 500 g. It is heated from 10°C to 45°C. The final density, taking the mass as constant and α_iron = 1.1×10⁻⁵ K⁻¹, is
explanation_steps: Initial volume is 2000 cm³, so the initial density is 0.25 g/cm³.
Volume expansion changes the volume by about 0.12%, which does not change the density at the printed precision. Answer: A.

questions.stem: A gas has a volume of 1.75 L at 80 cm Hg and 31°C. It is heated to twice that Celsius temperature and expands to 1.89 L. The final pressure is
explanation_steps: Twice the initial Celsius temperature is 62°C = 335 K, and 31°C = 304 K.

questions.stem: An ideal gas has a volume of 0.38 m³, a temperature of 34°C and a pressure of 3.0×10⁵ Pa. If the volume stays constant and the pressure becomes 4.0×10⁵ Pa, the temperature is
explanation_steps: At constant volume, T2 = 307 K × (4.0/3.0) = 409.3 K.

questions.stem: A 600 g metal block at 120°C is mixed with 300 g of water at 25°C in a 400 g calorimeter of specific heat 424.8 J·kg⁻¹·K⁻¹. The final temperature is 35°C. The specific heat of the metal, in J·kg⁻¹·K⁻¹, is (c_water = 4200 J·kg⁻¹·K⁻¹)
explanation_steps: Heat gained by water and calorimeter equals heat lost by the metal.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is wrong concerning the states of matter?

options.A: A solid melts at a definite temperature when heat is supplied.
options.B: Conversion of a solid directly to a gas is called evaporation.
options.C: Temperature, pressure, surface area and a draught affect the rate of evaporation.
options.D: Impurities can change the boiling point of a liquid.

explanation_steps: Direct conversion from solid to gas is sublimation, not evaporation.
The other statements are acceptable at this level. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Choose the incorrect statement.

options.A: The electric force law depends on distance in the same way as the gravitational force law.
options.B: The force between two point charges is unchanged if a third point charge is brought near them.
options.C: The force exerted by the field of a point charge q on another charge q′ is independent of q′.
options.D: Lines of force begin on a positive charge and end on a negative charge.
options.E: The number of lines of force per unit area is proportional to the electric field.

explanation_steps: The force on q′ is F = q′E, so it depends on q′.
The other statements match the inverse-square law, superposition as stated, and field-line conventions. Answer: C.

questions.stem: An electron starts from rest in a constant electric field of 3×10⁵ N/C. Its speed after 10⁻⁸ s is
explanation_steps: v = at = 5.27×10⁸ m/s. Answer: A.

questions.stem: Capacitors of 5×10⁻⁶ F, 4×10⁻⁶ F and 9×10⁻⁶ F are connected in series. The equivalent capacitance, in μF, and the charge on each capacitor, in μC, when a 9 V battery is connected across them are
explanation_steps: Series capacitors carry the same charge Q = CV = 1.78×9 = 16.0 μC. Answer: D.

questions.stem: A proton and a deuteron (mass twice the proton mass, same charge) move perpendicular to a magnetic field with equal kinetic energy. The deuteron orbit has radius 16.0 cm. The proton orbit radius is
explanation_steps: r = √(2mK)/(qB). Equal charge and kinetic energy give r ∝ √m.

questions.stem: A straight wire at the equator lies east–west. Earth’s field there is 3×10⁻⁵ T and the wire’s mass per unit length is 5×10⁻³ kg/m. The current that makes the magnetic force balance the weight is
explanation_steps: At the equator the horizontal field is perpendicular to an east–west wire.

questions.stem: A single-turn square coil, 0.25 m on a side, is perpendicular to a constant magnetic field. An emf of 15 mV is induced when its area decreases at 0.1 m²/s. The field magnitude is
explanation_steps: |ε| = B|dA/dt| for a single turn with the field perpendicular to the plane.

questions.stem: A spring has force constant 400 N/m. The work done to stretch it 3.0 cm from equilibrium, and the work done to stretch it from x = 2.0 cm to x = 3.0 cm, are
explanation_steps: Work from equilibrium is ½kx² = ½×400×(0.03)² = 0.18 J.
From 2.0 cm to 3.0 cm the work is ½k(0.03² − 0.02²) = 0.10 J. Answer: A.

questions.stem: Choose the incorrect statement.

options.A: In simple harmonic motion the acceleration is always opposite the displacement.
options.B: The period of oscillation is independent of the amplitude.
options.D: The total mechanical energy is conserved for damped vibrations.
options.E: For a given mass, the period of a spring–mass system is inversely proportional to √k.

explanation_steps: Damping removes mechanical energy, so the total mechanical energy is not conserved.
The other statements are standard SHM results. Answer: D.

questions.stem: At a crosswalk the siren of an approaching car is heard at 510 Hz. After the car passes, the frequency is 430 Hz. The car’s speed is (speed of sound = 343 m/s)
explanation_steps: The ratio of approaching to receding frequency is (v+vo)/(v−vo) = 510/430.

questions.stem: A 600 kg weather balloon is to lift a 4000 kg package. What helium volume is needed? (helium density 0.178 kg/m³, air density 1.29 kg/m³)
explanation_steps: Buoyancy equals the total weight: V(1.29 − 0.178) = 4600.
V = 4.14×10³ m³. Answer: B.

questions.stem: A copper bar is moved to the right with its axis perpendicular to a magnetic field. If the top of the bar becomes positive relative to the bottom, the magnetic field is

options.C: in the plane of the page, to the left.
options.D: in the plane of the page, to the right.

explanation_steps: Positive charges are driven upward, so v × B is upward with v to the right.
That requires B into the page. Answer: B.

questions.stem: A ball thrown vertically upward is caught at the same height after 3.5 s. Its initial velocity and maximum height are (g = 9.8 m/s²)
explanation_steps: Time of flight is 2u/g, so u = 3.5×9.8/2 = 17.2 m/s.
Maximum height is u²/(2g) = 15.0 m. Answer: A.

questions.stem: A student of mass 60 kg stands at the edge of a circular platform of moment of inertia 200 kg·m² and radius 2 m. The angular velocity is 2 rad/s at the edge. When the student is 0.5 m from the centre, the angular velocity is
explanation_steps: Angular momentum is conserved: (200 + 60×2²)×2 = (200 + 60×0.5²)ω.
ω = 880/215 = 4.09 rad/s. Answer: E.

questions.stem: Two stars of masses M and 4M are separated by a distance d. The distance from M to the point where the force on a third mass is zero is
explanation_steps: Between the stars, GMm/r² = G(4M)m/(d−r)².
d−r = 2r, so r = d/3 from M. Answer: B.

questions.stem: At the surface of Phobos, g is 0.001 times Earth’s g. If you can jump 2 m high on Earth, how high can you jump on Phobos, and how long does it take to reach that height?
explanation_steps: The same takeoff speed gives height inversely proportional to g, so the height is 2000 m.
Takeoff speed is √(2×9.8×2) = 6.26 m/s, and time to the top is v/g_Phobos = 639 s. Answer: E.

questions.stem: The dimension of the volt in base units of length, mass, time and current is
explanation_steps: One volt is one joule per coulomb.
[V] = M L² T⁻² / (A T) = M L² T⁻³ A⁻¹. Answer: A.

questions.stem: A nucleus has 90 protons and 144 neutrons. After emitting two beta particles followed by an alpha particle, it will have
explanation_steps: Each beta emission raises the proton number by 1 and lowers the neutron number by 1, giving 92 protons and 142 neutrons.
An alpha particle then removes 2 protons and 2 neutrons, leaving 90 protons and 140 neutrons. Answer: C.
